What makes Velociraptor so amazing?

Small but clever and quick, the Velociraptor was actually a dinosaur that had feathers. It looked a little different from the way it appears in the movies.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Velociraptor

In a 2007 study, quill knobs (marks where feathers attach) were found on a fossil forearm bone, showing that Velociraptor had feathers. It couldn't fly, though — the feathers were probably used for body-temperature control, courtship, and keeping eggs warm. With the sickle-shaped claw on its second toe, it gripped its prey tightly, and it had a large brain for its body and good night vision. Its top speed is estimated at about 40 km/h.

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Compare together: "The raptor in the movies has no feathers, but the real one did." Look for similarities to a bird's claws and feathers, and talk about how "birds are the descendants of dinosaurs" to spark even more interest.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Did Velociraptor really have feathers?
A. Yes. Marks where feathers attach (quill knobs) were found on fossils. It couldn't fly, though.

Q. What was the sickle-shaped claw used for?
A. The claw on its second toe was used to grip prey tightly — similar to the way hawks and eagles do.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Compare the movie raptor with the real one, and look for what it has in common with a bird's claws and feathers.
